knowledge_point.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+\frac{1}{3}y &=\frac{29}{3} \\ 3x+\frac{1}{5}y &=\frac{29}{5}.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{29}{3} \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & \frac{29}{5}\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{29}{3} \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & \frac{29}{5}\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{29}{3} \\ 0 & -\frac{4}{5} & -\frac{116}{5}\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{5}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{29}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 29\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+\frac{1}{3}y &=\frac{29}{3} \\ y &=29,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=29$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+\frac{1}{3}(29)=\frac{29}{3}\,⇒\,x=\frac{29}{3}-\frac{29}{3}=0.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=0$ and $y=29.$
